LESSON: WRITING 9.4.1 PUNCTUATION - THE COMMA

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade three
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 9
Topic 9.4: Writing 9.4.1 Punctuation - The Comma
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 9.4.1 Punctuation - The Comma, part of Strand 9 in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade three ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: How do we decide where to pause when reading a text?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 9.4.1 Punctuation - The Comma together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Communication and collaboration: Teamwork is developed as the learner actively participates in role play conversations with peers observing the rules

of engagement.

Values:
Love is cultivated as the learner portrays a caring attitude towards the peers as they work together.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life skills (Self-esteem): The learner’s self-esteem is nurtured as they use the commas correctly in writing.

Links to other Learning Areas:
The learner links the concept of comma to learning of similar concept in Kiswahili and Indigenous Language Activities.

Suggested Learning Resources

• Print textbooks in appropriate font size and colour contrast

• Braille books

• Digital devices with assistive technology,

• Charts, flash cards or braille cards,

• Pictures or picture description
